To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proposed inference rules are sufficient to update information states and provide a formal treatment of the basic reasoning mechanisms involved in information-oriented dialogue; (2) the proposed model is able to account for the basic phenomena of dialogue, such as the interpretation of questions and assertions; and (3) the proposed model can be extended with additional inference rules to cover other aspects of dialogue, such a presuppositions.

(a) a model of dialogue based on the notion of discourse obligations can be developed in the framework of information states; (b) a set of practical rules can be defined to update information states incrementally; (c) this set of rules allows us to assign intentional structures to dialogue moves and to account for a variety of phenomena in dialogue; and (d) the proposed model is not restricted to a specific type of dialogue and can be applied to a wide range of situations.

we have shown that a formal framework of discourse obligations, combined with a suitable formalism of information states and a set of practical rules for updating information states, can be used to model a wide range of dialogue phenomena, including the treatment of questions, answers, and assertions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how a formal model of information states can be used to capture the dynamics of discourse obligations in dialogue.
the question of whether the formal framework of discourse obligations can provide the basis for a general model of information-oriented dialogue.
developing a formal model of discourse obligations which is able to explain and predict the structure of dialogue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model is a promising first step towards a formal dialogue model which can account for a broad range of phenomena in human interaction.
the model presented here provides a framework for a dialogue theory which can be used to describe and explain the basic mechanisms of human dialogue.
the proposed framework provides a solid basis for the analysis of dialogue phenomena and can be extended to account for more complex dialogue structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our approach is able to account for many aspects of information-oriented dialogue in terms of discourse obligations and that it provides a natural framework for incremental updates of information states in a formal model.
we are able to account for the information flow in dialogue by means of a formal framework of discourse obligations.

we have developed a framework for the formal analysis of discourse obligations in dialogue which allows for a natural treatment of questions and answers, and which is capable of accounting for some of the basic phenomena of discourse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of discourse obligation can be used to model a wide range of dialogue phenomena in a uniform and principled fashion.

an obligation-driven dialogue model is a viable alternative to other approaches to dialogue modelling, and that it can be implemented in a way that is both tractable and flexible enough to be used in practical systems.
the notion of an information state can provide a suitable basis for a formal treatment of dialogue, even though it is not sufficient for an adequate analysis.
